sections.text: O Arjuna! The aspects of My divine life are endless. I have mentioned but a few by way of illustration.
Whatever is glorious, excellent, beautiful and mighty, be assured that it comes from a fragment of My splendour.
But what is the use of all these details to thee? O Arjuna! I sustain this universe with only small part of Myself.

We have been discussing chapter 10, and we are coming to its conclusion. So far we have seen that Bhagavan has been hammering on the same idea which has been discussed many times before in the Bhagavad Gita: that I am the source of all things and beings. The central theme of the Bhagavad Gita is that there is unity in diversity.
Even though we see this world as a world of plurality , each individual different from each other, each thing different from each other , there is an unseen thread running through all things and beings, because they all come from the same source. So there is similarity, there is something common to all. Thats basically Bhagavans theme.
All throughout the Bhagavad Gita, he has been explaining that in various ways. And we have seen in the beginning of this chapter, Bhagawan reiterated: Aham Sarvasya Prabhavah Matta Sarva Pravartate , I am the source of all beings and everything proceeds from me. It is something like a scientist would say: everything started from the Big Bang in our universe, and everything which we see in this universe came from the Big Bang.
So when you and I are nothing but the product of the Big Bang , when there was nothing but hydrogen and helium, and now we have all this complex universe that we are trying to understand. If somebody comes out and says, Thats all good, but explain to me how I can see evidence of the Big Bang in the universe, then people can start explaining: what you see in the galaxies , the hydrogen, the microwave radiation , it all comes from that original source. But you still have to give some examples.
So here Arjuna says the same thing: I understood that everything comes from that supreme reality, You, the supreme reality. Many sages in the past have said the same thing, and you are also now saying it. Im not doubting those sages, nor do I have any doubt in you.
But can you give me some examples in my life where I can feel your presence in the world of objects and beings? Thats what Bhagawan has given , 54 examples, somewhat reluctantly. Alas, I explained all of this, but you still want to know. Its like we all can learn the Bhagavad Gita and say that God is everywhere. God has no form, God is not a man, hes not a woman. But that doesnt end it.
I still want Bhagavans Darshan, because we are stuck with our perception of reality. Our perception is limited by our mind, intellect, and senses. We also want to see Bhagavan in the image which we have created in our mind.
Arjuna says the same thing. Show me evidence of your presence in my world. Bhagavan has given these 54 examples, starting from Vedic entities to Puranic ones, then natural phenomena and everything else you can think about, including some negative ones , Dandaha Damayatam Asmi, and among all the cheating and gambling.
He wanted to convey to Arjuna: I am not just in the good; everything thats seemingly evil in your world also exists only because I exist. And then the last few verses are the conclusion of this chapter, where Bhagawan says: I have exhausted the examples which I can give you, but there is not really any end to this discussion. You cant continue to say, Just give me one more example, just give me one more example. So he says: Yat cha Api Sarva Bhutanam Bijam Tat Aham Arjuna , whatever is the source of anything, I am that.
Because anything in this world, as we have described, is an effect. When I see something which I can perceive through my senses, its an effect. There has to be a cause, there has to be a source.
You see a child , you know there are parents for that child. A child cannot exist without parents. So the parents are the source of the child.
We see a pizza , we know there is a pizza maker somewhere. So everything we know has a source. And right now our conclusion is that everything has different sources.
Wood comes from somewhere, steel comes from somewhere else. Then all this comes together and we build buildings. Bhagawan here says that whatever you see in this world is a being. Being means that which has existence, that which comes into being, which comes into existence in this space and time.
I am the source, no matter what you see. Yat cha Api Sarvabhutanam Bijam, Tad Aham Arjuna. I am the primordial cause for all things and beings.
We understand this analogy of a seed and anything which comes out of it , a tree, an animal, a human being from a seed. But in that case, the seed is destroyed. After that manifestation is completed, when the tree comes into existence, that seed is gone.
But in this case, that seed is immutable. It remains as the support for that manifestation. So that cause remains as support for the effect.
There are three laws of causation,. One of them says: if you remove the cause from the effect, the effect does not remain. You remove the cause from this universe, which is the Supreme Being, and the universe does not remain.
The gold is the cause for the gold ornament. You remove the gold from the gold ornament, and the gold ornament does not remain. Na Tad Asti Vina Yat Syat maya Bhutam Characharam.
Without me, the moving or unmoving cannot exist in this world. Just as if we remove the gold, the gold ornament cannot exist. So Bhagawan has basically concluded that all these examples are given for you to understand and to train your mind to start seeing things as they are.
Theyre all made up of the same material. This universe has one source. Eventually you can trace down the source to that one entity which remains immutable , the uncaused cause.
There is no source for that cause. If you find a source for that cause, you can go further and find that source. So at one point in time, there will be a cause which has no cause.
So therefore Bhagavan said, I am that cause. And without that, nothing can exist. You remove that from this universe , its like in my dream.
My own thoughts are the source of my dream. But when I go into deep sleep, that dream cannot exist. Because without my mind, which is the source, the dream cannot exist.
Bhagawan here says the conclusion of all my examples is: I am the ultimate cause. I am the ultimate source of all things and beings. No thing, moving or unmoving, can exist without me.
This is the very efficient way in Vedanta to explain that everything is included , when you say moving and unmoving, all sentient beings and all inert things are included. Nothing can exist without my presence. There is no end to my Vibhuti.
You cannot count all the manifestations. If you want to catalog all the manifestations of physical world, in this physical world, even thats not possible. So now we have in our science all this Webb telescope so we can see as far as possible.
But lets say you want to catalog all the galaxies and all the stars in this universe. No matter what kind of a telescope you will have. There are billions and billions of stars and millions and millions of galaxies.
Its almost impossible. And by the time you catalog all of them, the new galaxies are formed and new stars are born, new old stars. Its a continuous change.
Therefore, in Sanskrit its called Jagat universe. But Jagat is that which is constantly changing. Something which is constantly changing, there is no end to its manifestation.
If its constantly changing, you cannot count it. But by the time you catalog what you have known, new things come into existence. We were in high school, we thought, if I learn this physics and chemistry, then Ill be good at it.
Well, physics and chemistry keeps changing in my own lifetime, so even that is not possible. Na antah asti mama divyanaam vibhuti nam paranti. But there is no end to the divine glories, the physical manifestation of myself.
But I told you some in detail just because you asked for it. Now you can figure out rest by yourself. Basically you teach somebody how to think, then the person can think himself rather than spoon feeding him.
Give them example and then a person can learn on his own how to detect that. If you figure out if you are working in a jewelry shop and you figure out how to test a gold ornament, whether it is gold or not, once you have one example, you can then apply that on any other example. So taking all these 54 examples, you have seen the method that anything which you see which has some excellence, thats because of the presence of that Lord.
Now I told you all that you should be able to detect this. But in conclusion I can tell you. Yat Vibhuti mat satvam Srimat urjitam eva va tattat eva avagatschatvam mama tej ansa sambhavah.
Whatever you see in this world, the world of your experiences, Jagat is not just the physical world which is changing outside the world of my experiences, world of my perception that is changing constantly, whatever in your perception, in your experience, you see as Vibhuti mat which has glory or its own excellence, Sattvam existence Sat is which is real, asat which is unreal. So Sattvam one context purity also that which has existence Srimat prosperous And Urjitam energetic. So anything which you see in this world, in nature, in society, in your community, in your family, where you see these qualities, you should know that they are all coming from me alone.
Tatta Eva Avagacvam Mama Teja Ansa Sambhavam. Its coming into existence because iota of my being. So dont consider that if I add up all this manifestation someday with some supercomputer and add it up, that will be Bhagavan.
He said no, no, that will be just an iota of my being. Gives a very good example that my mind has all the capabilities. But once in a while it gets confused or deluded by some random thought.
And then it goes into a wrong direction. It creates this scenario which is unrealistic. That doesnt mean I completely have lost all my ability to think.
My 99% of my ability is still valid. But right now its dormant. Its covered by the one delusion.
But when that one delusion is removed, 100% of my ability will be back. So Bhagavan is Satchitananda is ever pure. But this manifestation, the prakriti, the world of plurality comes into existence by just one part which creates this disturbance which they call the Hiranyagarva cumulative Vasanas.
Of all the beings and things which are in this universe, that one portion is now creating a new world. So when I go to sleep, my world comes to an end. In a deep sleep there is no world.
I dont exist, world does not exist. But my Vasras are there in dormant form. That dormant vasanas will find the appropriate condition.
My body has rested fully. I will wake up and they will all come back and manifest and create my own world. In case of Ishvara also, Ishwara remains as pure as brahman.
But all the cumulative asanas of of the Jagat are still in a dormant form.

The chapter concludes with a teaching that shatters our usual way of thinking about God and world. After 54 examples, Krishna says: Na antah asti mama divyanam vibhutinam - there is no end to My divine glories. And then the stunning finale: Vishtabhya aham idam kritsnam ekamshena sthito jagat - I support this entire universe with a single fragment of Myself. All we see - every star, every being, every atom - is sustained by just a portion of the divine. The infinite remainder lies beyond our comprehension entirely.
This teaching serves two purposes. First, it prevents worship of manifestations as the ultimate - no matter how glorious something appears, it is only a fragment pointing to the whole. Second, it instills appropriate awe - if this vast, incomprehensible universe is merely one-fraction, what must the whole be? Like a single thread of a tapestry that goes on forever, what we experience is real but partial. Our task is not to catalog all divine manifestations (impossible) but to recognize the principle: wherever there is excellence, beauty, power, or truth, there is divine presence.
Today, let this teaching reshape your perception. Look at everything you consider magnificent - towering mountains, brilliant minds, acts of extraordinary love - and remember: this is one fragment. The divine is not exhausted by any manifestation, no matter how grand. This should humble us (we cannot fully grasp the whole) and liberate us (we need not search elsewhere - the fragment before us is enough for recognition). Ask yourself: If everything glorious I have ever witnessed is only a fragment, what does this tell me about seeking more versus appreciating what is present? How would my life change if I truly saw each moment as a window onto the infinite?
